title: Diego Arria: “La destrucción de la hacienda La Carolina es reflejo del país”
content: Cuando el economista y político Diego Arria habla de La Carolina hace una larga pausa y le tiembla la voz. Es menos que imposible olvidar el despojo del que fue víctima en 2010 cuando el expresidente Hugo Chávez le arrebató ese terruño que se consolidaba como una intención de país. Para él, se trata

why_adverse: The article is an interview about dispossession. Diego Arria's family estate was seized by the Venezuelan state in 2010, stripped, and now stands in ruins; he frames it explicitly as a mirror of the country's destruction, and the piece ends on an ICC complaint and a decade of restoration work that has not happened. The filter scored rootedness 8.17 — the highest of its six dimensions — on the elegy the piece opens with: the 1850 colonial house, the tile roofs, La Bodeguita selling fresh cheese and milk on the mountain road. That rootedness is the thing the article reports as destroyed. Belonging read the remembered place as a present one. Note the trap in the ranking: raw 6.36 sits above this batch's p99 of 5.10, but percentile normalization mapped it to 6.54 and tier medium, so the lens looks moderate while the article is in fact near the top of its own population.
misleading_features: loving, present-tense description of a place and its rituals (the shop, the cheese, the chapel)
multigenerational family framing — the estate named after a dead daughter
